name: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), Regulation (EU) 2022/2554
description: All 64 articles of the Regulation, each with its official heading, chapter and a one-line summary. The article text is not reproduced.
source_note: Official Journal L 333, 27 December 2022, as published by the Publications Office of the European Union.

controls.title: Subject matter
controls.description: Sets the subject matter: uniform requirements on ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing, third-party risk and information sharing for financial entities, plus the oversight of critical ICT third-party providers.
controls.category: Chapter I: General provisions

controls.title: Scope
controls.description: Lists the financial entities in scope (banks, payment and e-money institutions, investment firms, insurers, crypto-asset service providers, trading venues and others) and the entities that are excluded.
controls.category: Chapter I: General provisions

controls.title: Definitions
controls.description: Defines the terms used, including digital operational resilience, ICT risk, ICT-related incident, major incident, critical or important function, TLPT and ICT third-party service provider.
controls.category: Chapter I: General provisions

controls.title: Proportionality principle
controls.description: Requires financial entities to apply the ICT risk rules in proportion to their size, risk profile and the nature, scale and complexity of their services.
controls.category: Chapter I: General provisions

controls.title: Governance and organisation
controls.description: The management body defines, approves and oversees the ICT risk management framework, is accountable for it, sets roles, budget, strategy and reporting lines, and must keep up its own ICT risk knowledge.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: ICT risk management framework
controls.description: Requires a documented ICT risk management framework with strategies, policies, procedures and tools that protect information and ICT assets, reviewed at least yearly and after major incidents, with an ICT business continuity strategy and a digital resilience strategy.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: ICT systems, protocols and tools
controls.description: Financial entities use and maintain up-to-date ICT systems, protocols and tools that are appropriate, reliable, resilient under stress and sized for their operations.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Identification
controls.description: Identify, classify and document ICT-supported business functions, information assets and ICT assets and their dependencies, keep the inventory current, and assess risks, legacy systems and third-party dependencies.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Protection and prevention
controls.description: Continuously monitor and secure ICT systems, minimise ICT risk through security tools and policies, and protect data in transit and at rest with strong authentication, access control, patching and change management.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Detection
controls.description: Put in place mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activity, performance issues and incidents, with defined alert thresholds and criteria that trigger response processes.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Response and recovery
controls.description: Maintain an ICT business continuity policy and response and recovery plans, tested at least yearly, covering the activation of response measures, crisis communication and recovery of critical functions.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Backup policies and procedures, restoration and recovery procedures and methods
controls.description: Develop backup policies and procedures, restoration and recovery procedures and methods, test them periodically, keep backup systems segregated, and meet recovery time and recovery point objectives.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Learning and evolving
controls.description: Gather information on vulnerabilities, threats and incidents, review after major incidents, train staff on digital resilience and learn lessons so the framework keeps evolving.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Communication
controls.description: Have crisis communication plans for responsible disclosure of major incidents and vulnerabilities, and a designated person to carry out the public and media function.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Further harmonisation of ICT risk management tools, methods, processes and policies
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities develop common technical standards that specify further the ICT security policies, procedures, protocols and tools, the risk management framework and the content of the continuity and recovery plans.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: Simplified ICT risk management framework
controls.description: Gives a simplified ICT risk management framework for small and non-interconnected investment firms, exempted payment and e-money institutions and similar entities, in place of Articles 5 to 15.
controls.category: Chapter II: ICT risk management

controls.title: ICT-related incident management process
controls.description: Define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process: record incidents and significant cyber threats, assign roles, escalate, and communicate to management, staff, clients and authorities.
controls.category: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting

controls.title: Classification of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats
controls.description: Classify ICT-related incidents and cyber threats by clients and transactions affected, duration, geographic spread, data losses, criticality of services and economic impact.
controls.category: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting

controls.title: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
controls.description: Report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority with an initial notification, an intermediate report and a final report, inform affected clients, and allow voluntary notification of significant cyber threats.
controls.category: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting

controls.title: Harmonisation of reporting content and templates
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities develop common technical standards and templates for the content of incident reports and notifications of significant cyber threats.
controls.category: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting

controls.title: Centralisation of reporting of major ICT-related incidents
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities report on the feasibility of centralising major-incident reporting through a single EU hub.
controls.category: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting

controls.title: Supervisory feedback
controls.description: Competent authorities acknowledge initial notifications and reports and give feedback and guidance, and pass relevant anonymised information to other authorities.
controls.category: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting

controls.title: Operational or security payment-related incidents concerning credit institutions, payment institutions, account information service providers, and electronic money institutions
controls.description: Extends the incident management, classification and reporting rules to operational or security payment-related incidents at credit institutions, payment institutions, account information service providers and e-money institutions.
controls.category: Chapter III: ICT-related incident management, classification and reporting

controls.title: General requirements for the performance of digital operational resilience testing
controls.description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, maintain a sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme as part of the ICT risk management framework, with tests carried out at least yearly on critical systems.
controls.category: Chapter IV: Digital operational resilience testing

controls.title: Testing of ICT tools and systems
controls.description: The testing programme includes appropriate tests such as vulnerability assessments, network security assessments, gap analyses, source code reviews, scenario-based tests and penetration testing, carried out by independent parties.
controls.category: Chapter IV: Digital operational resilience testing

controls.title: Advanced testing of ICT tools, systems and processes based on TLPT
controls.description: Entities identified by authorities carry out advanced threat-led penetration testing at least every three years on live production systems that support critical or important functions, including those of ICT third-party providers.
controls.category: Chapter IV: Digital operational resilience testing

controls.title: Requirements for testers for the carrying out of TLPT
controls.description: Testers for threat-led penetration testing must be suitable and reputable, technically capable, certified or formally accredited, insured and independent, and internal testers are limited to every third test.
controls.category: Chapter IV: Digital operational resilience testing

controls.title: General principles
controls.description: Financial entities manage ICT third-party risk within their risk framework: keep a register of contractual arrangements, assess risk before contracting, require exit strategies, and stay fully responsible for compliance.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk at entity level
controls.description: Before contracting ICT services for critical or important functions, assess whether the arrangement would create concentration risk through substitutability limits or multiple arrangements with the same or closely connected providers.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Key contractual provisions
controls.description: ICT service contracts must set out the parties' rights and obligations in writing, with service levels, locations, data protection, access and recovery, incident assistance, audit and termination rights and exit provisions.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Designation of critical ICT third-party service providers
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities designate the ICT third-party service providers that are critical for financial entities and appoint a Lead Overseer for each.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Structure of the Oversight Framework
controls.description: Establishes the Oversight Forum as a sub-committee of the Joint Committee to support the Lead Overseers and the oversight of critical ICT third-party providers.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Tasks of the Lead Overseer
controls.description: Sets the tasks of the Lead Overseer: assess whether each critical provider has rules, procedures and mechanisms to manage ICT risk, and issue oversight plans and recommendations.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Operational coordination between Lead Overseers
controls.description: Requires the three Lead Overseers to coordinate through a joint oversight network for a consistent approach to oversight of critical providers.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Powers of the Lead Overseer
controls.description: Gives the Lead Overseer powers to request information, conduct investigations and inspections, and address recommendations to critical ICT third-party providers.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Exercise of the powers of the Lead Overseer outside the Union
controls.description: Allows the Lead Overseer to exercise its powers on premises outside the Union where oversight objectives cannot be met within the Union.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Request for information
controls.description: The Lead Overseer may require critical providers to supply all information needed for oversight, by request or by decision, with periodic penalty payments for non-compliance.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: General investigations
controls.description: The Lead Overseer may conduct general investigations of critical providers, including examining records, taking statements and requesting explanations.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Inspections
controls.description: The Lead Overseer may carry out on-site inspections at the premises of critical providers, announced in advance except in urgent cases.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Ongoing oversight
controls.description: Joint examination teams from the supervisory authorities and national authorities support the Lead Overseer in continuing oversight of each critical provider.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Harmonisation of conditions enabling the conduct of the oversight activities
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities develop technical standards on the information critical providers must submit, oversight conduct and the conditions for joint examination teams.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Follow-up by competent authorities
controls.description: Critical providers notify the Lead Overseer within 60 days whether they will follow its recommendations, and competent authorities may require financial entities to take measures where they do not.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Oversight fees
controls.description: The Lead Overseer charges critical ICT third-party service providers fees that cover the costs of oversight.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: International cooperation
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities may conclude administrative arrangements with third-country authorities to cooperate on ICT third-party risk.
controls.category: Chapter V: Managing of ICT third-party risk

controls.title: Information-sharing arrangements on cyber threat information and intelligence
controls.description: Financial entities may exchange cyber threat information and intelligence among themselves within trusted communities, under conditions that protect personal data and business confidentiality, and must notify authorities of participation.
controls.category: Chapter VI: Information-sharing arrangements

controls.title: Competent authorities
controls.description: Names the competent authorities responsible for ensuring compliance with this Regulation for each type of financial entity.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Cooperation with structures and authorities established by Directive (EU) 2022/2555
controls.description: The authorities cooperate with the structures established under the NIS2 Directive, including the Cooperation Group, CSIRTs and single points of contact.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Cooperation between authorities
controls.description: Competent authorities and the Lead Overseer cooperate closely and exchange information relating to critical ICT third-party service providers.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Financial cross-sector exercises, communication and cooperation
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities may organise financial cross-sector exercises, communication and cooperation to test response and recovery.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Administrative penalties and remedial measures
controls.description: Competent authorities hold the supervisory, investigatory and sanctioning powers needed, including access to documents, on-site inspections, orders to cease conduct and administrative penalties.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Exercise of the power to impose administrative penalties and remedial measures
controls.description: Competent authorities exercise their penalty powers directly, in collaboration, by delegation or by application to judicial authorities, taking account of the gravity of the breach.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Criminal penalties
controls.description: Member States may decide not to lay down administrative penalties for breaches that are subject to criminal penalties and must make sure appropriate measures are in place.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Notification duties
controls.description: Member States notify the Commission and the European Supervisory Authorities of the national laws implementing the penalty provisions and of later amendments.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Publication of administrative penalties
controls.description: Competent authorities publish decisions imposing administrative penalties on their official websites, with provision for anonymised or delayed publication where needed.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Professional secrecy
controls.description: Confidential information received under this Regulation is covered by professional secrecy, binding persons who work or have worked for the authorities.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Data Protection
controls.description: The European Supervisory Authorities and competent authorities may process personal data only where necessary to carry out their duties under this Regulation, in line with EU data protection law.
controls.category: Chapter VII: Competent authorities

controls.title: Exercise of the delegation
controls.description: Governs how the Commission exercises its power to adopt delegated acts: five-year period, revocation, notification to Parliament and Council and the objection period.
controls.category: Chapter VIII: Delegated acts

controls.title: Review clause
controls.description: The Commission reviews the Regulation by 17 January 2028 and reports to the European Parliament and Council, covering the designation criteria for critical providers, the testing regime and the interaction with other law.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Transitional and final provisions

controls.title: Amendments to Regulation (EC) No 1060/2009
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EC) No 1060/2009 on credit rating agencies so that their ICT risk is managed under this Regulation.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Transitional and final provisions

controls.title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) No 648/2012
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 (EMIR) so that central counterparties and trade repositories meet this Regulation's ICT requirements.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Transitional and final provisions

controls.title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) No 909/2014
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) No 909/2014 so that central securities depositories manage operational and ICT risk under this Regulation.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Transitional and final provisions

controls.title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) No 600/2014
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 so that approved publication arrangements and similar providers meet this Regulation's ICT requirements.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Transitional and final provisions

controls.title: Amendment to Regulation (EU) 2016/1011
controls.description: Amends Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 so that administrators of critical benchmarks manage ICT systems under this Regulation.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Transitional and final provisions

controls.title: Entry into force and application
controls.description: Provides that the Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after publication and applies from 17 January 2025.
controls.category: Chapter IX: Transitional and final provisions
